leads.name: Witte moerbei (White Mulberry) at the Van Abbemuseum
leads.reason: Register (LRMB nr 1690223, reason 'dendrologisch', age unknown) says monumental, but the Gemeente Eindhoven open-data 'bomen' dataset shows a Morus alba 1.4m from this point classed only 'Waardevol' (valuable), not 'Monumentaal', and planted 1970 (about 55 years old, not old by this project's bar). Sources conflict on both age and status; no visual or narrative evidence found that it is otherwise spectacular. Worth a second look if a photo or a stronger account turns up, but as it stands it does not clear the 'worth the walk' bar on its own.

leads.name: Papier moerbei (Paper Mulberry), Stadswandelpark
leads.reason: Only the LRMB register (nr 1690255, planted_band 1920-1930) places a tree here. The Gemeente Eindhoven open-data 'bomen' dataset has exactly one Papiermoerbei citywide, and it sits about 50m away near the Van Abbemuseum area (boomnummer 61975, planted 2002, 'Waardevol'), not at this coordinate, so it is not the same tree. A 60m radius search of the municipal dataset around this point found no paper mulberry at all (found instead a cluster of 1960-planted ginkgos, dawn redwoods and swamp cypresses, an arboretum-like planting near the Sterrenwacht). Two searches for independent confirmation (web search, municipal open data) came up empty. Second source not found; do not ship on the register alone.

leads.name: Spaanse eik (likely Northern Red Oak) near the Sterrenwacht, Stadswandelpark
leads.species: possibly Northern Red Oak (Quercus rubra); unconfirmed
leads.reason: Only the LRMB register (nr 1690256, planted_band 1930-1940, place given only as '* Nabij de Sterrenwacht, Stadspark, Eindhoven', visible='onbekend') places a tree here; the asterisk in the register's own place field suggests even the register is uncertain about the exact spot. No matching 'Spaanse eik' entry exists anywhere in the Gemeente Eindhoven open-data 'bomen' dataset citywide (checked by name, zero hits), and a 150m radius search around this coordinate found no Quercus rubra either, only a 1960s-era conifer/ginkgo planting. Web search found nothing specific. Second source not found and even the register's own location is marked uncertain; leave for a future pass with a site visit or better register scan.

leads.name: Pluimiep, Frederika van Pruisenweg
leads.species: possibly Zelkova or a plume-form elm cultivar; register gives no scientific name

location.address: Frederika van Pruisenweg, opposite nos. 2 and 58, Villapark, Eindhoven

leads.reason: LRMB register nr 1690252, planted_band 1900-1910, visitable=ja, but its own n_trees field says 7. That reads as a row or small stand rather than one collectible point (CLAUDE.md's rule: an avenue or a whole stand of trees is blocked, an entry must be one identifiable tree). Left as a lead rather than blocked outright because a site visit might find one standout specimen among the seven worth publishing on its own; a future pass with photos or a map of the individual trunks could settle it.
sources_checked: Gemeente Eindhoven open data 'bomen' geosearch within 25m of the point, no match found

leads.name: Hongaarse eik PSV-stadion

location.address: Frederiklaan 61, near gate 11 of the Philips Stadium, Eindhoven

leads.reason: Only the LRMB register (nr 1697320, planted_band 1910-1920, visitable=ja, visible=ja, status 1) places a Hungarian oak here. A web search for corroboration surfaced a genuinely different, well-documented monumental tree nearby instead: a white horse chestnut on Frederiklaan south of the stadium that is the subject of a supporters' memorial art project (psv.nl), which is not this tree and should not be confused with it or with the already-published ein_001 (a horse chestnut at Frederiklaan 10a, gate 11). No second source found specifically for the Hungarian oak. Worth a second look; it sits about 500m from ein_001 so could extend that corner of the walk if confirmed.
sources_checked: WebSearch: "Hongaarse eik" Frederiklaan Eindhoven PSV stadion boom

leads.name: Extra trees of Sint Trudo churchyard (Strijpsestraat 129), beyond the already-published copper beech (ein_008)
leads.species: mixed: copper beech (Fagus sylvatica f. purpurea), a variant labelled 'Slangenden' (species unclear from the register)

location.address: Strijpsestraat 129, kerkhof Sint Trudokerk, Strijp, Eindhoven

leads.reason: The LRMB register lists several more entries at this same churchyard beyond nr 1694310 (already published as ein_008): nr 1680249 'Bruine beuk' explicitly carries n_trees=17, clearly a grove or hedge rather than one collectible point, and is blocked for that reason (see blocked list). Two more, nr 1695441 (bruine beuk, n_trees=2) and nr 1695440 (bruine beuk, n_trees not distinct), and nr 1680251 ('Slangenden', n_trees=2, an unclear register name, possibly corrupted text, standing in the former rectory's front garden) sit within roughly 150m of ein_008 and of each other. All are marked visitable=ja by the register but none has a recognition feature in the register data that would let a visitor tell it apart from ein_008 or from each other without standing there; publishing several near-identical copper beeches in one churchyard risks exactly the 'which trunk is worth the visit' problem this project tries to avoid (CLAUDE.md, the Nigatsu-do case). Left as a lead for a future pass with photos or a site visit that can describe what makes any one of them distinct.
